newsitem.title: USA: NYC economy still weak on job growth - McCall.
newsitem.headline: NYC economy still weak on job growth - McCall.

text.p: New York City's private sector employment growth slowed in the third quarter of 1996 after rising more rapidly in the first half of the year, according to a report released by state Comptroller H. Carl McCall.
The report said that while job growth is slowing, the city economy had benefited from Wall Street's boom that led to gains in income and tax revenues.
The report also noted that jobs in culture, media and tourism continue to expand.

McCall, however, cautioned that "after seeing new jobs grow by an average of almost 5,000 permonth from January to June, expansion has slowed to just 1,000 jobs per month from July through September."
The Boroughs of the Bronx, Brooklyn and Queens have regained two-thirds of the jobs lost in the recent recession, the report said.
